subject: gulper eel
title: This Deep-Sea Eel Is Mostly Mouth, and It Eats Tiny Shrimp

scenes.text: This eel can balloon its mouth until it looks bigger than its body.
The gulper eel lives up to three thousand metres down, in total darkness.
Its jaws can stretch to about half its body length, and its stomach stretches too.
The tail tip glows pink, a lure in the black water.
You'd expect something huge to fall in. Mostly, it's small crustaceans.
The giant mouth is a net, not a weapon. It swallows the ocean and keeps the snacks.

description:
The gulper or pelican eel lives roughly 500 to 3,000 metres deep, grows to about 1 metre and has jaws reaching half its body length or more, plus a glowing tail tip.
Despite the enormous mouth, it mainly eats small crustaceans, expanding its throat and stomach to take in food and water. In 2018 the E/V Nautilus filmed one inflating its mouth off Hawaii.
What would you want to see from the deep sea next?
first_comment: In 2018 a research ship filmed a gulper eel puffing its mouth up like a balloon, nearly a mile down. What should we look at next?
